name: Update all packages
description: Refresh the package index and upgrade every installed Termux package in one pass. Run this regularly so dependencies stay compatible.

steps.title: Update and upgrade
steps.description: The two commands are chained so the upgrade uses the freshest index. Review the package list before confirming.

name: Install a package
description: Install Git from the Termux repository and confirm the binary is available. The same pattern works for most CLI tools.

steps.title: Install Git
steps.description: The -y flag accepts the dependency prompt. Remove it if you prefer to review every prompt.

steps.title: Verify the install
steps.description: Printing the version proves the binary is on PATH.

name: Search the package repository
description: Find packages by name or description without installing anything. Useful when you only remember part of a tool's name.

steps.title: Search for Python tools
steps.description: Replace python with another keyword to explore a different area.

name: List installed packages
description: See exactly what is installed in your Termux prefix. Handy before removing tools or comparing two devices.

steps.title: Print installed packages
steps.description: Pipe through less if the list is long: pkg list-installed | less.

name: Remove a package
description: Uninstall a tool and then remove orphaned dependencies. Replace the example package name with your own before running.

steps.title: Uninstall the package
steps.description: The example removes cowsay. Change the name to the package you want to remove.

steps.title: Remove unused dependencies
steps.description: This only removes packages that nothing else depends on.

name: Clean the package cache
description: Free space by deleting cached .deb files. Installed packages are not affected.

steps.title: Clean cached packages
steps.description: Termux can re-download anything it needs later.

name: Install proot-distro
description: proot-distro runs full Linux distributions without root. Install it once, then add the distributions you need.

steps.title: Install the helper
steps.description: proot-distro manages downloads, login shells and removal for you.

steps.title: Check the version
steps.description: Confirm the command is available.

name: List available distributions
description: See which distributions can be installed and which ones already exist on this device.

steps.title: Show the catalogue
steps.description: The output marks installed distributions and their aliases.

name: Install Ubuntu
description: Download and unpack an Ubuntu root filesystem. This can take several minutes and needs a stable connection.

steps.title: Install Ubuntu
steps.description: Keep the app open while the root filesystem downloads.

steps.title: Confirm it is installed
steps.description: The list now shows ubuntu as installed.

name: Enter Ubuntu
description: Open an interactive Ubuntu shell from Termux. Your Termux home is available at /root in many proot setups, but check before relying on it.

steps.title: Log in
steps.description: Type exit inside Ubuntu to return to Termux.

name: Remove an installed distribution
description: Permanently delete a proot root filesystem and everything inside it. Back up files you need before confirming.

steps.title: Remove the root filesystem
steps.description: This deletes the Ubuntu installation. Files stored outside it are untouched.

name: Create a shell alias
description: Save keystrokes with a permanent alias. This example makes ll print a detailed directory listing.

steps.title: Add the alias
steps.description: The single quotes are preserved in .bashrc exactly as written.

steps.title: Reload the shell
steps.description: Open a new session or source the file now.

name: Customize the shell prompt
description: Show the user, host and working directory in every Bash prompt. The change is written to .bashrc and survives restarts.

steps.title: Write a new PS1
steps.description: The escaped codes are expanded by Bash each time a prompt is drawn.

steps.title: Apply it
steps.description: Reload the file in the current session.

name: Write your first Bash script
description: Create a small script that fails fast and prints a message. The heredoc writes the file without touching your editor.

steps.title: Create hello.sh
steps.description: Every newline and quote in the heredoc is preserved.
steps.command:
cat > hello.sh <<'EOF'
#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "Hello from Termux"
EOF

steps.title: Make it executable
steps.description: A script needs the executable bit before it can be launched directly.

steps.title: Run it
steps.description: The output should be: Hello from Termux

name: Loop over log files
description: Iterate through matching files and process each one. This is a safer starting point than parsing ls output.

steps.title: Run the loop
steps.description: If no .log files exist, the literal pattern is skipped by the nullglob suggestion below.
steps.command:
shopt -s nullglob
for file in *.log; do
  echo "Processing $file"
done

steps.title: Make globbing permanent
steps.description: Optional: keep nullglob enabled in future shells.

name: Lint a shell script
description: Catch quoting and portability mistakes before a script runs. ShellCheck explains every finding with a link.

steps.title: Install ShellCheck
steps.description: A small package that pays for itself quickly.

steps.title: Check your script
steps.description: Replace hello.sh with the file you want to inspect.

name: Set up shared storage
description: Give Termux access to Android's shared storage so you can open files from Downloads and other folders. Android will ask for permission.

steps.title: Request access
steps.description: Accept Android's permission dialog. Shared storage appears under ~/storage/shared.

steps.title: List the links
steps.description: Folders such as downloads, dcim and shared are created if permission was granted.

name: Find large files and folders
description: Sort the current directory by size so you can see what is using space. Review the list before deleting anything.

steps.title: Show the largest entries
steps.description: Change ~ to another folder to inspect it instead of your home directory.

name: Search text inside files
description: Find a string recursively with line numbers. Useful for projects and configuration files.

steps.title: Search a folder
steps.description: Replace TODO with your search term and ~/projects with the folder to scan.

name: Create a compressed archive
description: Package a project folder into a dated .tar.gz archive. The original files stay in place.

steps.title: Build the archive
steps.description: The filename includes today's date. Adjust the folder name.

steps.title: Verify it exists
steps.description: Check the size before moving the archive somewhere else.

name: Extract a tar archive
description: Unpack a .tar.gz file into the current directory. Run it inside an empty folder if you do not know the archive contents.

steps.title: List the contents first
steps.description: Reviewing entries prevents surprises before extraction.

steps.title: Extract
steps.description: Replace the filename with the archive you want to unpack.

name: Extract a zip file
description: Install unzip and inspect an archive before writing its files. Useful for downloads from shared storage.

steps.title: Install unzip
steps.description: Termux does not always include unzip by default.

steps.title: Inspect the archive
steps.description: Check the paths before extracting.

steps.title: Extract
steps.description: Files are written relative to the current directory.

name: Check disk usage
description: See remaining space and the size of top-level folders. This helps diagnose failed installs and downloads.

steps.title: Show free space
steps.description: The Use% column shows how full each mount is.

steps.title: Show folder sizes
steps.description: Only top-level entries in your home directory are measured.

name: Set your Git identity
description: Configure the name and email written into every commit. Use the address attached to your Git hosting account.

steps.title: Set your name
steps.description: Replace the example name before running.

steps.title: Set your email
steps.description: Replace the example address with the one your host recognizes.

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Both values should be printed.

name: Clone a repository
description: Download a Git repository and enter it. This example uses Termux's public app repository.

steps.title: Clone
steps.description: HTTPS cloning works without an SSH key. Private repositories need authentication.

steps.title: Enter the folder
steps.description: Inspect the README before building or modifying anything.

name: Daily Git workflow
description: Review, stage and commit changes with a clear message. Follow your project's contribution rules before committing.

steps.title: Check status
steps.description: See which files changed before staging anything.

steps.title: Review the diff
steps.description: Read the changes. Add individual paths instead of . when you want more control.

steps.title: Stage and commit
steps.description: Replace the example message with a short description of the change.
steps.command: git add . && git commit -m "Describe the change"

name: Publish a new repository
description: Turn a folder into a Git repository and push it to an empty remote. Create the empty remote on your Git host first.

steps.title: Initialize locally
steps.description: Run this inside the project folder.
steps.command: git init && git add . && git commit -m "Initial commit"

steps.title: Rename the branch
steps.description: Many hosts expect main.

steps.title: Add the remote
steps.description: Replace the example URL with your empty repository.

steps.title: Push
steps.description: Your host will ask for authentication. Never paste a password into a shared script.

name: Create an SSH key
description: Generate an Ed25519 key for Git hosting or servers. The private key never leaves your device; only copy the public key.

steps.title: Install OpenSSH
steps.description: Skip if ssh-keygen is already available.

steps.title: Generate the key
steps.description: Press Enter to accept the default path, then choose a passphrase.

steps.title: Print the public key
steps.description: Copy only the .pub line into your account settings. Never share id_ed25519.

name: Install Python
description: Install Python 3 and confirm the interpreter and package manager work. Termux packages are not the same as Android system Python.

steps.title: Install Python
steps.description: This includes pip.

steps.title: Check both tools
steps.description: Both commands should print a version.

name: Create a Python virtual environment
description: Keep project dependencies isolated from the system Python. Activate the environment before installing packages.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.description: Run this inside your project folder.

steps.title: Activate it
steps.description: Your prompt usually changes while the environment is active.

steps.title: Upgrade pip
steps.description: Install dependencies only after activation.

name: Install project requirements
description: Recreate a Python environment from a requirements file. Activate the virtual environment first.

steps.title: Install the requirements
steps.description: The file must exist in the current directory.

steps.title: Freeze the resolved versions
steps.description: Optional: write exact versions back to the file for reproducible installs.

name: Install Node.js
description: Install the LTS Node.js runtime and npm. Avoid building native modules until their build tools are installed.

steps.title: Install Node.js LTS
steps.description: The package name is nodejs-lts in Termux.

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Both Node and npm should report versions.

name: Start a Node project
description: Create a package manifest and install Express. Run npm init inside an empty project folder.

steps.title: Create package.json
steps.description: The -y flag accepts the defaults.

steps.title: Install Express
steps.description: Dependencies are written to package.json and node_modules.

name: Serve a folder over HTTP
description: Share files on your local network with Python's built-in server. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.description: Run it in the folder to share. Open http://localhost:8000 on the device, or the device IP from another machine on the same network.

name: Install a C compiler
description: Install Clang and verify it can compile a trivial program. This is the starting point for many native builds.

steps.title: Install Clang
steps.description: The package also pulls in the linker and standard headers.

steps.title: Check the version
steps.description: Printing the version confirms the toolchain is on PATH.

name: Search code with ripgrep
description: ripgrep is faster and friendlier than grep for source trees. It respects ignore files such as .gitignore by default.

steps.title: Install ripgrep
steps.description: The binary is named rg.

steps.title: Search the current project
steps.description: Replace TODO with your pattern.

name: Connect to a server over SSH
description: Open an interactive shell on a remote machine. Host keys are verified on first connection, so read the fingerprint prompt carefully.

steps.title: Install OpenSSH
steps.description: Skip if ssh is already available.

steps.title: Connect
steps.description: Replace the example user and host. SSH will prompt for a password or use your key.

name: Copy a file to a server
description: Upload a local file to a remote home directory with scp. Replace the example host and filename before running.

steps.title: Upload the file
steps.description: The trailing colon separates the host from the remote path.

name: Start an SSH server in Termux
description: Accept SSH connections to your device on a local network. Set a strong password and only enable this on networks you trust.

steps.title: Install OpenSSH
steps.description: The package includes both the client and server.

steps.title: Set a password
steps.description: Choose a long, unique password. The username is printed by whoami.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.description: Termux sshd listens on port 8022 by default. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

name: Download a file with curl
description: Download over HTTPS and keep the server's filename. Verify downloaded files before running or opening them.

steps.title: Download
steps.description: The -L flag follows redirects. Replace the example URL.

steps.title: Check the result
steps.description: A non-zero size is a good first sign that the download completed.

name: Test network connectivity
description: Check HTTPS responses and DNS resolution when installs or syncs fail. Both commands are read-only.

steps.title: Check an HTTPS endpoint
steps.description: Look for a 2xx or 3xx status line.

steps.title: Check DNS
steps.description: Install dnsutils first if nslookup is missing: pkg install dnsutils -y.

name: Find your public IP
description: Ask a public service for the address your connection appears to use. This is not stored by the app and may be shared with your ISP.

steps.title: Query the address
steps.description: The service sees your request; use it only when needed.

name: Inspect running processes
description: See what Termux and its child processes are doing. Use this when a background job will not stop or a build is stuck.

steps.title: List processes
steps.description: The PID column is what you pass to kill if a process must be stopped.

steps.title: Filter for one program
steps.description: Replace python with the process name you are looking for.

name: Check memory and load
description: See available RAM and current load before running a heavy build. Termux shares memory with Android, so leave headroom.

steps.title: Show memory
steps.description: The available column is the most useful number for headroom.

steps.title: Show load
steps.description: Load is sampled over 1, 5 and 15 minutes.

name: Inspect the Termux environment
description: Collect the Termux version, architecture and prefix paths. Useful when reporting a problem or choosing a package build.

steps.title: Show Termux information
steps.description: Review the output for the version and architecture fields.

steps.title: Show the architecture
steps.description: Common values are aarch64, arm and x86_64.

name: Send a completion notification
description: Ask Android to show a notification when a long job finishes. Requires the Termux:API app and the termux-api package.

steps.title: Install the API package
steps.description: The Termux:API companion app must also be installed from the official releases.

steps.title: Send a test notification
steps.description: Android may ask for notification permission the first time.

name: Read and write the clipboard
description: Move short text between Termux and Android without retyping it. Requires Termux:API.

steps.title: Put text on the clipboard
steps.description: The text is placed on Android's clipboard for other apps.

steps.title: Read it back
steps.description: This prints the current clipboard contents; treat it as sensitive if you copied a secret.

name: Check battery status
description: Read the battery level, charging state and temperature with Termux:API. Useful in scripts that should pause on low battery.

steps.title: Query the battery
steps.description: The output is JSON, which is easy to parse in a script.

name: Keep Termux awake
description: Hold a wake lock while a long download or build runs. Release it when finished so Android can manage battery normally.

steps.title: Acquire a wake lock
steps.description: Android will keep the CPU available while this lock is held.

steps.title: Release it
steps.description: Run this after the long task. Leaving a wake lock on drains the battery.

name: Audit listening ports
description: List TCP and UDP sockets that are accepting connections. Reviewing this helps you notice unexpected local services.

steps.title: Install net-tools
steps.description: Termux may not ship netstat by default.

steps.title: List listening sockets
steps.description: The -tulpn flags select TCP/UDP listeners and show ports; process names may require root.

name: Verify a downloaded file
description: Compare a SHA-256 checksum with the value published by the source. A mismatch means the download should not be used.

steps.title: Compute the hash
steps.description: Replace file.zip with the file you downloaded.

steps.title: Compare manually
steps.description: Read the published checksum from the vendor's official release page and compare every character. Do not trust a checksum sent over an unverified channel.

name: Inspect file permissions
description: Find world-writable files in your home directory. Unexpected permissions are worth investigating before sharing a backup.

steps.title: Find world-writable files
steps.description: The command only lists candidates; it does not change permissions.
